hypothesis: A rectangular footprint imposes unsupported corner wedges on observed convex buildings with oblique or clipped corners. A convex hull of the same robustly bounded observed XY support can reduce this geometric over-completion while preserving the convex clipping pipeline.
changed_behavior: Keep the existing minimum-rectangle orientation and projected quantile bounds.
When retained XY support has at least three distinct non-collinear points, replace the rectangle footprint with its counterclockwise convex hull.
Retain the rectangle fallback for insufficient support and record the selected footprint rule in model metrics.
expected_benefit: Avoid imposing orthogonal rectangular corners where the input supports a different convex boundary; roof clipping, walls and base all use the same selected footprint.
risks: Concave footprints and courtyards remain unsupported; K01 is addressed only for observed convex boundary shape.
Incomplete boundary observations may shrink the hull below the true building footprint.
Spurious points inside the existing quantile bounds can still expand the hull.
Additional boundary vertices can increase mesh complexity.

feedback_used.basis: Only initial_algorithm.py, knowledge.json and the no-outcome feedback.json were read.

model_configuration: inherited parent runtime; exact provider snapshot unavailable
scope: One isolated candidate proposal; not proof of general self-improvement.
